metadata.title: Palantir is a 'narrative play,' strategist explains

content.text:
Laffer Tengler Investments CEO and CIO Nancy Tengler shares her thoughts on Palantir (PLTR) stock and why it's a buy.
You want to own Palantir?
Yeah, we own it. We uh we own it in two strategies. Uh we've added to it during the summer swoon a few times.
We got a lot of chances to do it. And if you just think about that, during Deepseek, we we picked off some at $88 a share.
It ran way up and then it came back, but it was still a good investment from that standpoint. It's not a valuation play, it's a narrative play.
Uh but what do you mean by that, Nancy? It's it's it's it's a narrative play.
It's very expensive. Uh well, I I think they are in the sweet spot. Alex Karp came out on the call and said, uh we're the only company, the only company that is showing that is uh adding or realizing economic value from tokens.
And now he's building a front-end engine because he's really hyped up about the the large language models stealing his data.
So, I think that's going to become another business line for them.
When I when they reported, I had Gil Luria on the show, DA Davidson guy. I think Gil's a really smart guy. We were talking about the numbers and
I was looking it was 93% top line growth. US commercials was like 150%.
adjusted operating margin was north of 60. And I asked Gil about that. Now he's a bull, he's a believer. He told me, Nancy, he said, it might be the best company that is publicly traded. What do you make of that comment?
I I think he might be right. I mean, I I'd throw a couple others in there, but of the software names, this CEO knows how and when to pivot and he's a fighter.
And that that's what you want as an as an investor. You want somebody, you know, he's, he would not want to be compared to Elon Musk, I'm sure, but Elon Musk is that guy where you go, I don't know how he's going to do it, but he's going to succeed.
And that's that's definitely true for Alex Karp. So, but we also love the the the segment of the market they're in, the the consolidation of data for defense. Uh I think that's going to be a continue to be a growing market.
